Mat.9.18.kjv: While he spake these things unto them, behold, there came a certain ruler, and worshipped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live.

Mat.9.24.bsb: “Go away,” He told them. “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” And they laughed at Him.
Mat.9.24.kjv: He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.

Mat.9.25.bsb: After the crowd had been put outside, Jesus went in and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.
Mat.9.25.kjv: But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose.

Mat.9.26.bsb: And the news about this spread throughout that region.
Mat.9.26.kjv: And the fame hereof went abroad into all that land.

Mat.15.28.bsb: “O woman,” Jesus answered, “your faith is great! Let it be done for you as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that very hour.
Mat.15.28.kjv: Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.

Mat.17.18.bsb: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, and he was healed from that moment.
Mat.17.18.kjv: And Jesus rebuked the devil; and he departed out of him: and the child was cured from that very hour.

Mat.19.13.bsb: Then little children were brought to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them and pray for them. And the disciples rebuked those who brought them.
Mat.19.13.kjv: Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them.

Mat.19.14.bsb: But Jesus said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”
Mat.19.14.kjv: But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

Mat.19.15.bsb: And after He had placed His hands on them, He went on from there.
Mat.19.15.kjv: And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.

Mat.15.4.bsb: For God said, ‘Honor your father and mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’
Mat.15.4.kjv: For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.

Mat.19.19.bsb: honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.’”
Mat.19.19.kjv: Honour thy father and thy mother: and, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

Mat.18.4.bsb: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
Mat.18.4.kjv: Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

Mat.18.5.bsb: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.
Mat.18.5.kjv: And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.

Mat.15.5.bsb: But you say that if anyone says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is a gift devoted to God,’
Mat.15.5.kjv: But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me;

Mat.18.3.bsb: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
Mat.18.3.kjv: And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

Mat.21.15.bsb: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”
Mat.21.15.kjv: And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the Son of David; they were sore displeased,

Mat.21.16.bsb: “Do You hear what these children are saying?” they asked. “Yes,” Jesus answered. “Have you never read: ‘From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise’?”
Mat.21.16.kjv: And said unto him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?

Mat.18.2.bsb: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.
Mat.18.2.kjv: And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them,

Mat.18.6.bsb: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
Mat.18.6.kjv: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.

Mat.12.4.bsb: He entered the house of God, and he and his companions ate the consecrated bread, which was not lawful for them to eat, but only for the priests.
Mat.12.4.kjv: How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?

Mat.21.13.bsb: And He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’”
Mat.21.13.kjv: And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

Mat.4.5.bsb: Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.
Mat.4.5.kjv: Then the devil taketh him up into the holy city, and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple,

Mat.16.18.bsb: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
Mat.16.18.kjv: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

Mat.18.17.bsb: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.
Mat.18.17.kjv: And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.

Mat.12.28.bsb: But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Mat.12.28.kjv: But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.

Mat.19.24.bsb: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
Mat.19.24.kjv: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

Mat.21.31.bsb: Which of the two did the will of his father?” “The first,” they answered. Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God before you.
Mat.21.31.kjv: Whether of them twain did the will of his father? They say unto him, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.

Mat.3.2.bsb: and saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.”
Mat.3.2.kjv: And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Mat.4.17.bsb: From that time on Jesus began to preach, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.”
Mat.4.17.kjv: From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Mat.5.3.bsb: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Mat.5.3.kjv: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

Mat.5.10.bsb: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Mat.5.10.kjv: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

Mat.5.19.bsb: So then, whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do likewise will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
Mat.5.19.kjv: Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

Mat.5.20.bsb: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
Mat.5.20.kjv: For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.

Mat.16.28.bsb: Truly I tell you, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”
Mat.16.28.kjv: Verily I say unto you, There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.

Mat.21.41.bsb: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and will rent out the vineyard to other tenants who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time.”
Mat.21.41.kjv: They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render him the fruits in their seasons.

Mat.13.24.bsb: Jesus put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
Mat.13.24.kjv: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:

Mat.21.33.bsb: Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
Mat.21.33.kjv: Hear another parable: There was a certain householder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country:

Mat.21.34.bsb: When the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.
Mat.21.34.kjv: And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, that they might receive the fruits of it.

Mat.21.35.bsb: But the tenants seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.
Mat.21.35.kjv: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.

Mat.21.36.bsb: Again, he sent other servants, more than the first group. But the tenants did the same to them.
Mat.21.36.kjv: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them likewise.

Mat.21.37.bsb: Finally, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
Mat.21.37.kjv: But last of all he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.

Mat.21.38.bsb: But when the tenants saw the son, they said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’
Mat.21.38.kjv: But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance.

Mat.21.39.bsb: So they seized him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
Mat.21.39.kjv: And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.

Mat.21.40.bsb: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard returns, what will he do to those tenants?”
Mat.21.40.kjv: When the lord therefore of the vineyard cometh, what will he do unto those husbandmen?

Mat.21.43.bsb: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.
Mat.21.43.kjv: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.

Mat.21.44.bsb: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.”
Mat.21.44.kjv: And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

Mat.21.45.bsb: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they knew that Jesus was speaking about them.
Mat.21.45.kjv: And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them.

Mat.21.46.bsb: Although they wanted to arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the people regarded Him as a prophet.
Mat.21.46.kjv: But when they sought to lay hands on him, they feared the multitude, because they took him for a prophet.

Mat.12.6.bsb: But I tell you that One greater than the temple is here.
Mat.12.6.kjv: But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.

Mat.12.8.bsb: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
Mat.12.8.kjv: For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.

Mat.23.8.bsb: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
Mat.23.8.kjv: But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren.

Mat.23.10.bsb: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.
Mat.23.10.kjv: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your Master, even Christ.

Mat.16.15.bsb: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?”
Mat.16.15.kjv: He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am?

Mat.16.16.bsb: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Mat.16.16.kjv: And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.

Mat.16.17.bsb: Jesus replied, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.
Mat.16.17.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.

Mat.23.2.bsb: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
Mat.23.2.kjv: Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:

Mat.23.3.bsb: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.
Mat.23.3.kjv: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.

Mat.23.4.bsb: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
Mat.23.4.kjv: For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.

Mat.23.5.bsb: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.
Mat.23.5.kjv: But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,

Mat.23.6.bsb: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,
Mat.23.6.kjv: And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,

Mat.23.7.bsb: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.
Mat.23.7.kjv: And greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.

Mat.23.13.bsb: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.
Mat.23.13.kjv: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.

Mat.23.15.bsb: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are.
Mat.23.15.kjv: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.

Mat.23.25.bsb: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
Mat.23.25.kjv: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.

Mat.23.27.bsb: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.
Mat.23.27.kjv: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.

Mat.23.28.bsb: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.
Mat.23.28.kjv: Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

Mat.23.29.bsb: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.
Mat.23.29.kjv: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,

Mat.23.30.bsb: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’
Mat.23.30.kjv: And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.

Mat.23.31.bsb: So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
Mat.23.31.kjv: Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.

Mat.23.32.bsb: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers.
Mat.23.32.kjv: Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.

Mat.23.33.bsb: You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of hell?
Mat.23.33.kjv: Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?

Mat.26.14.bsb: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
Mat.26.14.kjv: Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests,

Mat.26.16.bsb: So from then on Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus.
Mat.26.16.kjv: And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.

Mat.26.59.bsb: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking false testimony against Jesus in order to put Him to death.
Mat.26.59.kjv: Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death;

Mat.26.60.bsb: But they did not find any, though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward
Mat.26.60.kjv: But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses,

Mat.26.61.bsb: and declared, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”
Mat.26.61.kjv: And said, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.

Mat.26.62.bsb: So the high priest stood up and asked Him, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”
Mat.26.62.kjv: And the high priest arose, and said unto him, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?

Mat.26.64.bsb: “You have said it yourself,” Jesus answered. “But I say to all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
Mat.26.64.kjv: Jesus saith unto him, Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

Mat.26.66.bsb: What do you think?” “He deserves to die,” they answered.
Mat.26.66.kjv: What think ye? They answered and said, He is guilty of death.

Mat.26.68.bsb: and said, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit You?”
Mat.26.68.kjv: Saying, Prophesy unto us, thou Christ, Who is he that smote thee?

Mat.16.19.bsb: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.”
Mat.16.19.kjv: And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

Mat.18.16.bsb: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
Mat.18.16.kjv: But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.

Mat.18.18.bsb: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
Mat.18.18.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

Mat.12.50.bsb: For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.”
Mat.12.50.kjv: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

Mat.8.11.bsb: I say to you that many will come from the east and the west to share the banquet with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
Mat.8.11.kjv: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.

Mat.11.11.bsb: Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
Mat.11.11.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

Mat.13.17.bsb: For truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous men longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
Mat.13.17.kjv: For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.

Mat.13.31.bsb: He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
Mat.13.31.kjv: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field:

Mat.13.32.bsb: Although it is the smallest of all seeds, yet it grows into the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.”
Mat.13.32.kjv: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.

Mat.13.33.bsb: He told them still another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”
Mat.13.33.kjv: Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

Mat.13.44.bsb: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again, and in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field.
Mat.13.44.kjv: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.

Mat.13.45.bsb: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls.
Mat.13.45.kjv: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:

Mat.13.46.bsb: When he found one very precious pearl, he went away and sold all he had and bought it.
Mat.13.46.kjv: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

Mat.27.29.bsb: And they twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on His head. They put a staff in His right hand, knelt down before Him, and mocked Him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
Mat.27.29.kjv: And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!

Mat.10.28.bsb: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
Mat.10.28.kjv: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

Mat.27.36.bsb: And sitting down, they kept watch over Him there.
Mat.27.36.kjv: And sitting down they watched him there;

Mat.27.37.bsb: Above His head they posted the written charge against Him: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Mat.27.37.kjv: And set up over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

Mat.27.38.bsb: Two robbers were crucified with Him, one on His right and the other on His left.
Mat.27.38.kjv: Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.

Mat.27.45.bsb: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
Mat.27.45.kjv: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.

Mat.27.47.bsb: When some of those standing there heard this, they said, “He is calling Elijah.”
Mat.27.47.kjv: Some of them that stood there, when they heard that, said, This man calleth for Elias.

Mat.27.48.bsb: One of them quickly ran and brought a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and held it up for Jesus to drink.
Mat.27.48.kjv: And straightway one of them ran, and took a spunge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.

Mat.27.49.bsb: But the others said, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.”
Mat.27.49.kjv: The rest said, Let be, let us see whether Elias will come to save him.

Mat.27.51.bsb: At that moment the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth quaked, and the rocks were split.
Mat.27.51.kjv: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;

Mat.27.52.bsb: The tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
Mat.27.52.kjv: And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,

Mat.27.53.bsb: After Jesus’ resurrection, when they had come out of the tombs, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.
Mat.27.53.kjv: And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many.

Mat.7.13.bsb: Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
Mat.7.13.kjv: Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:

Mat.7.17.bsb: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.
Mat.7.17.kjv: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

Mat.12.34.bsb: You brood of vipers, how can you who are evil say anything good? For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
Mat.12.34.kjv: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

Mat.12.35.bsb: The good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure, and the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure.
Mat.12.35.kjv: A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.

Mat.5.31.bsb: It has also been said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
Mat.5.31.kjv: It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:

Mat.5.32.bsb: But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, brings adultery upon her. And he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Mat.5.32.kjv: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery.

Mat.19.10.bsb: His disciples said to Him, “If this is the case between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry.”
Mat.19.10.kjv: His disciples say unto him, If the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry.

Mat.19.11.bsb: “Not everyone can accept this word,” He replied, “but only those to whom it has been given.
Mat.19.11.kjv: But he said unto them, All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given.

Mat.19.12.bsb: For there are eunuchs who were born that way; others were made that way by men; and still others live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.”
Mat.19.12.kjv: For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.

Mat.22.21.bsb: “Caesar’s,” they answered. So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
Mat.22.21.kjv: They say unto him, Cesar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cesar the things which are Cesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.

Mat.22.36.bsb: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”
Mat.22.36.kjv: Master, which is the great commandment in the law?

Mat.22.40.bsb: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”
Mat.22.40.kjv: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

Mat.7.12.bsb: In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.
Mat.7.12.kjv: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

Mat.9.10.bsb: Later, as Jesus was dining at Matthew’s house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Him and His disciples.
Mat.9.10.kjv: And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.

Mat.9.11.bsb: When the Pharisees saw this, they asked His disciples, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Mat.9.11.kjv: And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?

Mat.9.12.bsb: On hearing this, Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
Mat.9.12.kjv: But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.

Mat.9.13.bsb: But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
Mat.9.13.kjv: But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

Mat.23.9.bsb: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
Mat.23.9.kjv: And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven.

Mat.21.19.bsb: Seeing a fig tree by the road, He went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. “May you never bear fruit again!” He said. And immediately the tree withered.
Mat.21.19.kjv: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.

Mat.21.20.bsb: When the disciples saw this, they marveled and asked, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?”
Mat.21.20.kjv: And when the disciples saw it, they marvelled, saying, How soon is the fig tree withered away!

Mat.21.28.bsb: But what do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first one and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’
Mat.21.28.kjv: But what think ye? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard.

Mat.21.29.bsb: ‘I will not,’ he replied. But later he changed his mind and went.
Mat.21.29.kjv: He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.

Mat.21.30.bsb: Then the man went to the second son and told him the same thing. ‘I will, sir,’ he said. But he did not go.
Mat.21.30.kjv: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.

Mat.21.32.bsb: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him.
Mat.21.32.kjv: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.

Mat.15.1.bsb: Then some Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem and asked,
Mat.15.1.kjv: Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying,

Mat.15.3.bsb: Jesus replied, “And why do you break the command of God for the sake of your tradition?
Mat.15.3.kjv: But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition?

Mat.15.6.bsb: he need not honor his father or mother with it. Thus you nullify the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
Mat.15.6.kjv: And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.

Mat.15.7.bsb: You hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied correctly about you:
Mat.15.7.kjv: Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying,

Mat.15.8.bsb: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
Mat.15.8.kjv: This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.

Mat.15.9.bsb: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’”
Mat.15.9.kjv: But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

Mat.15.10.bsb: Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “Listen and understand.
Mat.15.10.kjv: And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:

Mat.15.11.bsb: A man is not defiled by what enters his mouth, but by what comes out of it.”
Mat.15.11.kjv: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.

Mat.15.12.bsb: Then the disciples came to Him and said, “Are You aware that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?”
Mat.15.12.kjv: Then came his disciples, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying?

Mat.15.13.bsb: But Jesus replied, “Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.
Mat.15.13.kjv: But he answered and said, Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.

Mat.15.15.bsb: Peter said to Him, “Explain this parable to us.”
Mat.15.15.kjv: Then answered Peter and said unto him, Declare unto us this parable.

Mat.15.16.bsb: “Do you still not understand?” Jesus asked.
Mat.15.16.kjv: And Jesus said, Are ye also yet without understanding?

Mat.15.17.bsb: “Do you not yet realize that whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and then is eliminated?
Mat.15.17.kjv: Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?

Mat.15.18.bsb: But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a man.
Mat.15.18.kjv: But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.

Mat.15.20.bsb: These are what defile a man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile him.”
Mat.15.20.kjv: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.

Mat.12.2.bsb: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to Him, “Look, Your disciples are doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath.”
Mat.12.2.kjv: But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.

Mat.12.3.bsb: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
Mat.12.3.kjv: But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;

Mat.12.5.bsb: Or haven’t you read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and yet are innocent?
Mat.12.5.kjv: Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?

Mat.12.7.bsb: If only you had known the meaning of ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the innocent.
Mat.12.7.kjv: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.

Mat.27.18.bsb: For he knew it was out of envy that they had handed Jesus over to him.
Mat.27.18.kjv: For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Mat.9.22.bsb: Jesus turned and saw her. “Take courage, daughter,” He said, “your faith has healed you.” And the woman was healed from that very hour.
Mat.9.22.kjv: But Jesus turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.

Mat.21.21.bsb: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.
Mat.21.21.kjv: Jesus answered and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done.

Mat.6.27.bsb: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
Mat.6.27.kjv: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?

Mat.6.28.bsb: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.
Mat.6.28.kjv: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

Mat.6.29.bsb: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
Mat.6.29.kjv: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

Mat.6.30.bsb: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?
Mat.6.30.kjv: Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?

Mat.6.31.bsb: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’
Mat.6.31.kjv: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

Mat.6.32.bsb: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
Mat.6.32.kjv: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

Mat.6.34.bsb: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.
Mat.6.34.kjv: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

Mat.17.19.bsb: Afterward the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
Mat.17.19.kjv: Then came the disciples to Jesus apart, and said, Why could not we cast him out?

Mat.17.20.bsb: “Because you have so little faith,” He answered. “For truly I tell you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.”
Mat.17.20.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.

Mat.1.19.bsb: Because Joseph her husband was a righteous man and was unwilling to disgrace her publicly, he resolved to divorce her quietly.
Mat.1.19.kjv: Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.

Mat.2.14.bsb: So he got up, took the Child and His mother by night, and withdrew to Egypt,
Mat.2.14.kjv: When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:

Mat.7.24.bsb: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
Mat.7.24.kjv: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:

Mat.7.25.bsb: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.
Mat.7.25.kjv: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

Mat.8.2.bsb: Suddenly a leper came and knelt before Him, saying, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
Mat.8.2.kjv: And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

Mat.8.13.bsb: Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go! As you have believed, so will it be done for you.” And his servant was healed at that very hour.
Mat.8.13.kjv: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.

Mat.11.28.bsb: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
Mat.11.28.kjv: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

Mat.11.29.bsb: Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
Mat.11.29.kjv: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

Mat.11.30.bsb: For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”
Mat.11.30.kjv: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

Mat.14.27.bsb: But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
Mat.14.27.kjv: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

Mat.17.7.bsb: Then Jesus came over and touched them. “Get up,” He said. “Do not be afraid.”
Mat.17.7.kjv: And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid.

Mat.8.5.bsb: When Jesus had entered Capernaum, a centurion came and pleaded with Him,
Mat.8.5.kjv: And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,

Mat.8.6.bsb: “Lord, my servant lies at home, paralyzed and in terrible agony.”
Mat.8.6.kjv: And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.

Mat.8.7.bsb: “I will go and heal him,” Jesus replied.
Mat.8.7.kjv: And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.

Mat.8.8.bsb: The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy to have You come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
Mat.8.8.kjv: The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.

Mat.8.9.bsb: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”
Mat.8.9.kjv: For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.

Mat.8.10.bsb: When Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those following Him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.
Mat.8.10.kjv: When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

Mat.9.21.bsb: She said to herself, “If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.”
Mat.9.21.kjv: For she said within herself, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.

Mat.14.33.bsb: Then those who were in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “Truly You are the Son of God!”
Mat.14.33.kjv: Then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.

Mat.15.26.bsb: But Jesus replied, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
Mat.15.26.kjv: But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.

Mat.15.27.bsb: “Yes, Lord,” she said, “even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.”
Mat.15.27.kjv: And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.

Mat.4.18.bsb: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Mat.4.18.kjv: And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.

Mat.4.19.bsb: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
Mat.4.19.kjv: And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

Mat.4.20.bsb: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
Mat.4.20.kjv: And they straightway left their nets, and followed him.

Mat.4.21.bsb: Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. Jesus called them,
Mat.4.21.kjv: And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.

Mat.4.22.bsb: and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.
Mat.4.22.kjv: And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him.

Mat.9.23.bsb: When Jesus entered the house of the synagogue leader, He saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.
Mat.9.23.kjv: And when Jesus came into the ruler’s house, and saw the minstrels and the people making a noise,

Mat.14.36.bsb: and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.
Mat.14.36.kjv: And besought him that they might only touch the hem of his garment: and as many as touched were made perfectly whole.

Mat.15.23.bsb: But Jesus did not answer a word. So His disciples came and urged Him, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.”
Mat.15.23.kjv: But he answered her not a word. And his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she crieth after us.

Mat.15.24.bsb: He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
Mat.15.24.kjv: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

Mat.15.25.bsb: The woman came and knelt before Him. “Lord, help me!” she said.
Mat.15.25.kjv: Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.

Mat.9.2.bsb: Just then some men brought to Him a paralytic lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.”
Mat.9.2.kjv: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.

Mat.15.21.bsb: Leaving that place, Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon.
Mat.15.21.kjv: Then Jesus went thence, and departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon.

Mat.14.25.bsb: During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.
Mat.14.25.kjv: And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea.

Mat.14.26.bsb: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified. “It’s a ghost!” they said, and cried out in fear.
Mat.14.26.kjv: And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear.

Mat.14.28.bsb: “Lord, if it is You,” Peter replied, “command me to come to You on the water.”
Mat.14.28.kjv: And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water.

Mat.14.29.bsb: “Come,” said Jesus. Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.
Mat.14.29.kjv: And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus.

Mat.14.30.bsb: But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid and, beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!”
Mat.14.30.kjv: But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.

Mat.14.31.bsb: Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter. “You of little faith,” He said, “why did you doubt?”
Mat.14.31.kjv: And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?

Mat.14.32.bsb: And when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.
Mat.14.32.kjv: And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased.

Mat.16.20.bsb: Then He admonished the disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ.
Mat.16.20.kjv: Then charged he his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ.

Mat.17.14.bsb: When they came to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt before Him.
Mat.17.14.kjv: And when they were come to the multitude, there came to him a certain man, kneeling down to him, and saying,

Mat.17.15.bsb: “Lord, have mercy on my son,” he said. “He has seizures and is suffering terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.
Mat.17.15.kjv: Lord, have mercy on my son: for he is lunatick, and sore vexed: for ofttimes he falleth into the fire, and oft into the water.

Mat.17.16.bsb: I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him.”
Mat.17.16.kjv: And I brought him to thy disciples, and they could not cure him.

Mat.17.17.bsb: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to Me.”
Mat.17.17.kjv: Then Jesus answered and said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him hither to me.

Mat.17.21.kjv: Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.

Mat.8.23.bsb: When He got into the boat, His disciples followed Him.
Mat.8.23.kjv: And when he was entered into a ship, his disciples followed him.

Mat.8.25.bsb: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!”
Mat.8.25.kjv: And his disciples came to him, and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we perish.

Mat.8.26.bsb: “You of little faith,” Jesus replied, “why are you so afraid?” Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm.
Mat.8.26.kjv: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.

Mat.8.27.bsb: The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the sea obey Him!”
Mat.8.27.kjv: But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!

Mat.18.21.bsb: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
Mat.18.21.kjv: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?

Mat.18.22.bsb: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
Mat.18.22.kjv: Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.

Mat.6.1.bsb: “Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
Mat.6.1.kjv: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.

Mat.6.3.bsb: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
Mat.6.3.kjv: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

Mat.6.4.bsb: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
Mat.6.4.kjv: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.

Mat.6.8.bsb: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
Mat.6.8.kjv: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

Mat.7.11.bsb: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!
Mat.7.11.kjv: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

Mat.10.20.bsb: For it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
Mat.10.20.kjv: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

Mat.10.29.bsb: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.
Mat.10.29.kjv: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.

Mat.10.32.bsb: Therefore everyone who confesses Me before men, I will also confess him before My Father in heaven.
Mat.10.32.kjv: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.

Mat.10.33.bsb: But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven.
Mat.10.33.kjv: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.

Mat.11.25.bsb: At that time Jesus declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.
Mat.11.25.kjv: At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.

Mat.11.26.bsb: Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
Mat.11.26.kjv: Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in thy sight.

Mat.18.14.bsb: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.
Mat.18.14.kjv: Even so it is not the will of your Father which is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.

Mat.20.23.bsb: “You will indeed drink My cup,” Jesus said. “But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them.”
Mat.20.23.kjv: And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.

Mat.26.29.bsb: I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s kingdom.”
Mat.26.29.kjv: But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.

Mat.26.42.bsb: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”
Mat.26.42.kjv: He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.

Mat.19.17.bsb: “Why do you ask Me about what is good?” Jesus replied. “There is only One who is good. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”
Mat.19.17.kjv: And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.

Mat.5.48.bsb: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Mat.5.48.kjv: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

Mat.6.18.bsb: so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
Mat.6.18.kjv: That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.

Mat.18.11.kjv: For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.

Mat.18.12.bsb: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?
Mat.18.12.kjv: How think ye? if a man have an hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and goeth into the mountains, and seeketh that which is gone astray?

Mat.18.13.bsb: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
Mat.18.13.kjv: And if so be that he find it, verily I say unto you, he rejoiceth more of that sheep, than of the ninety and nine which went not astray.

Mat.6.14.bsb: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
Mat.6.14.kjv: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

Mat.18.23.bsb: Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
Mat.18.23.kjv: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account of his servants.

Mat.18.24.bsb: As he began the settlements, a debtor owing ten thousand talents was brought to him.
Mat.18.24.kjv: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, which owed him ten thousand talents.

Mat.18.26.bsb: Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’
Mat.18.26.kjv: The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

Mat.18.27.bsb: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.
Mat.18.27.kjv: Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.

Mat.19.26.bsb: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
Mat.19.26.kjv: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.

Mat.3.9.bsb: And do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.
Mat.3.9.kjv: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

Mat.2.12.bsb: And having been warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they withdrew to their country by another route.
Mat.2.12.kjv: And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.

Mat.2.21.bsb: So Joseph got up, took the Child and His mother, and went to the land of Israel.
Mat.2.21.kjv: And he arose, and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.

Mat.2.22.bsb: But when he learned that Archelaus was reigning in Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. And having been warned in a dream, he withdrew to the district of Galilee,
Mat.2.22.kjv: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:

Mat.5.5.bsb: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
Mat.5.5.kjv: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.

Mat.20.15.bsb: Do I not have the right to do as I please with what is mine? Or are you envious because I am generous?’
Mat.20.15.kjv: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?

Mat.21.23.bsb: When Jesus returned to the temple courts and began to teach, the chief priests and elders of the people came up to Him. “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You this authority?”
Mat.21.23.kjv: And when he was come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came unto him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?

Mat.26.3.bsb: At that time the chief priests and elders of the people assembled in the courtyard of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas,
Mat.26.3.kjv: Then assembled together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, unto the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,

Mat.26.4.bsb: and they conspired to arrest Jesus covertly and kill Him.
Mat.26.4.kjv: And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him.

Mat.26.5.bsb: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”
Mat.26.5.kjv: But they said, Not on the feast day, lest there be an uproar among the people.

Mat.26.57.bsb: Those who had arrested Jesus led Him away to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
Mat.26.57.kjv: And they that had laid hold on Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled.

Mat.26.58.bsb: But Peter followed Him at a distance, right up to the courtyard of the high priest. And he went in and sat down with the guards to see the outcome.
Mat.26.58.kjv: But Peter followed him afar off unto the high priest’s palace, and went in, and sat with the servants, to see the end.

Mat.27.1.bsb: When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people conspired against Jesus to put Him to death.
Mat.27.1.kjv: When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death:

Mat.27.2.bsb: They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.
Mat.27.2.kjv: And when they had bound him, they led him away, and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor.

Mat.27.3.bsb: When Judas, who had betrayed Him, saw that Jesus was condemned, he was filled with remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.
Mat.27.3.kjv: Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,

Mat.27.4.bsb: “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood,” he said. “What is that to us?” they replied. “You bear the responsibility.”
Mat.27.4.kjv: Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that.

Mat.28.14.bsb: If this report reaches the governor, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble.”
Mat.28.14.kjv: And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and secure you.

Mat.27.24.bsb: When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that instead a riot was breaking out, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd. “I am innocent of this man’s blood,” he said. “You bear the responsibility.”
Mat.27.24.kjv: When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.

Mat.22.17.bsb: So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
Mat.22.17.kjv: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not?

Mat.22.18.bsb: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?
Mat.22.18.kjv: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?

Mat.22.19.bsb: Show Me the coin used for the tax.” And they brought Him a denarius.
Mat.22.19.kjv: Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny.

Mat.22.20.bsb: “Whose image is this,” He asked, “and whose inscription?”
Mat.22.20.kjv: And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?

Mat.3.11.bsb: I baptize you with water for repentance, but after me will come One more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
Mat.3.11.kjv: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire:

Mat.4.1.bsb: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
Mat.4.1.kjv: Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.

Mat.16.26.bsb: What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
Mat.16.26.kjv: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

Mat.19.16.bsb: Just then a man came up to Jesus and inquired, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?”
Mat.19.16.kjv: And, behold, one came and said unto him, Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?

Mat.5.1.bsb: When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to Him,
Mat.5.1.kjv: And seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain: and when he was set, his disciples came unto him:

Mat.5.2.bsb: and He began to teach them, saying:
Mat.5.2.kjv: And he opened his mouth, and taught them, saying,

Mat.5.4.bsb: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
Mat.5.4.kjv: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

Mat.5.6.bsb: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
Mat.5.6.kjv: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.

Mat.5.7.bsb: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
Mat.5.7.kjv: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

Mat.5.8.bsb: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Mat.5.8.kjv: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

Mat.5.11.bsb: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me.
Mat.5.11.kjv: Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.

Mat.5.14.bsb: You are the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden.
Mat.5.14.kjv: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.

Mat.5.17.bsb: Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them.
Mat.5.17.kjv: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.

Mat.5.18.bsb: For I tell you truly, until heaven and earth pass away, not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen, will disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.
Mat.5.18.kjv: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.

Mat.5.21.bsb: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not murder’ and ‘Anyone who murders will be subject to judgment.’
Mat.5.21.kjv: Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:

Mat.5.23.bsb: So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
Mat.5.23.kjv: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee;

Mat.5.24.bsb: leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother; then come and offer your gift.
Mat.5.24.kjv: Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.

Mat.5.25.bsb: Reconcile quickly with your adversary, while you are still on the way to court. Otherwise, he may hand you over to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.
Mat.5.25.kjv: Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.

Mat.5.26.bsb: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.
Mat.5.26.kjv: Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou hast paid the uttermost farthing.

Mat.5.27.bsb: You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’
Mat.5.27.kjv: Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery:

Mat.5.28.bsb: But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
Mat.5.28.kjv: But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.

Mat.5.29.bsb: If your right eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
Mat.5.29.kjv: And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.

Mat.5.30.bsb: And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to depart into hell.
Mat.5.30.kjv: And if thy right hand offend thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.

Mat.5.33.bsb: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’
Mat.5.33.kjv: Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:

Mat.5.34.bsb: But I tell you not to swear at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;
Mat.5.34.kjv: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne:

Mat.13.47.kjv: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:

Mat.11.20.bsb: Then Jesus began to denounce the cities in which most of His miracles had been performed, because they did not repent.
Mat.11.20.kjv: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:

Mat.11.7.bsb: As John’s disciples were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
Mat.11.7.kjv: And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

Mat.11.8.bsb: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings’ palaces.
Mat.11.8.kjv: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.

Mat.11.9.bsb: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
Mat.11.9.kjv: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet.

Mat.12.43.bsb: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it.
Mat.12.43.kjv: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none.

Mat.11.2.bsb: Meanwhile John heard in prison about the works of Christ, and he sent his disciples
Mat.11.2.kjv: Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples,

Mat.9.14.bsb: Then John’s disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast so often, but Your disciples do not fast?”
Mat.9.14.kjv: Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast oft, but thy disciples fast not?

Mat.13.55.bsb: “Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t His mother’s name Mary, and aren’t His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
Mat.13.55.kjv: Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?

Mat.13.56.bsb: Aren’t all His sisters with us as well? Where then did this man get all these things?”
Mat.13.56.kjv: And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?

Mat.9.16.bsb: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. For the patch will pull away from the garment, and a worse tear will result.
Mat.9.16.kjv: No man putteth a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse.

Mat.18.7.bsb: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!
Mat.18.7.kjv: Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!

Mat.15.38.bsb: A total of four thousand men were fed, besides women and children.
Mat.15.38.kjv: And they that did eat were four thousand men, beside women and children.

Mat.12.40.bsb: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
Mat.12.40.kjv: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

Mat.10.16.bsb: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.
Mat.10.16.kjv: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

Mat.9.34.bsb: But the Pharisees said, “It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons.”
Mat.9.34.kjv: But the Pharisees said, He casteth out devils through the prince of the devils.

Mat.22.28.bsb: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? For all of them were married to her.”
Mat.22.28.kjv: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.

Mat.9.38.bsb: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”
Mat.9.38.kjv: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.

Mat.13.27.bsb: The owner’s servants came to him and said, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?’
Mat.13.27.kjv: So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares?

Mat.9.33.bsb: And when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”
Mat.9.33.kjv: And when the devil was cast out, the dumb spake: and the multitudes marvelled, saying, It was never so seen in Israel.

Mat.19.28.bsb: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, in the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Mat.19.28.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

Mat.3.15.bsb: “Let it be so now,” Jesus replied. “It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way.” Then John permitted Him.
Mat.3.15.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him.

Mat.17.27.bsb: “But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a four-drachma coin. Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.”
Mat.17.27.kjv: Notwithstanding, lest we should offend them, go thou to the sea, and cast an hook, and take up the fish that first cometh up; and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a piece of money: that take, and give unto them for me and thee.

Mat.12.29.bsb: Or again, how can anyone enter a strong man’s house and steal his possessions, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can plunder his house.
Mat.12.29.kjv: Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.

Mat.9.8.bsb: When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
Mat.9.8.kjv: But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men.
